evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryUserRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository implement the domain ProjectRepository, UserRepository and TaskRepository interfaces; filtering exists only in findByProject

src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: TaskController takes TaskService through its constructor and calls only service methods; it checks statuses with the domain's isTaskStatus; parsing is centralized in readString, requiredString and requiredParam; errorHandler is the single place that maps errors to HTTP statuses
src/infrastructure/server.ts: createApp is the composition root; it builds TaskService from the in-memory repositories and mounts TaskController.router and errorHandler
Minor: the message 'Status must be todo, in_progress, or done' in TaskController.createTask hard-codes the status names, but the actual check still goes through isTaskStatus
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The three files are one coherent infrastructure adapter layer. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the persistence adapters: InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryUserRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository each implement a domain repository interface. task-controller.ts holds the HTTP adapter: TaskController routes requests to TaskService, and errorHandler turns errors into HTTP responses. server.ts is the composition root: createApp wires the repositories and the controller into TaskService and Express. The files use the module's abstractions consistently. server.ts builds everything through the exported classes. The controller depends only on TaskService and never touches the repositories directly. It checks statuses with the domain's isTaskStatus instead of keeping its own copy of the status values. Task filtering lives only in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProject. Request parsing goes through one set of helpers (readString, requiredString, requiredParam), and error mapping is centralized in errorHandler. One small issue: the message "Status must be todo, in_progress, or done" spells out the status names by hand. That is a cosmetic repeat of the domain's status list, not a second copy of the rule itself, so it doesn't fail the rubric.
